title: Parity versus \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\) with shallow quantum preprocessing
formal: Does every polynomial-size constant-depth classical \(\mathrm{AC}^0\) circuit with polynomial-size constant-depth quantum preprocessing have asymptotically zero correlation with parity? Precisely, for every polynomial \(p\), constant \(d\in\mathbb N\), and sequence \((C_n,f_n)_{n\ge1}\) satisfying the model and bounds below, is \[\left|2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\ \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n+m(n)}}\Pr[C_n(x)=y]f_n(y)(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^nx_i}\right|\longrightarrow0\quad(n\longrightarrow\infty)?\] Here \(m(n)\le p(n)\) zero-initialized ancillary qubits are allowed, both circuit stages have depth at most \(d\), and both have polynomial size bounded by \(p(n)\). There is no geometric locality, uniformity or clean-ancilla condition.

source_formulation.text: \(\mathrm{AC}^0\circ\mathrm{QNC}^0\) cannot maintain constant correlation with parity as the input length grows.
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of Conjecture3, retaining its nonuniform arbitrary-two-qubit-gate model

why: Parity is a basic test of global information processing. Resolving this conjecture would show whether very shallow quantum preprocessing can give weak classical decision circuits a persistent advantage on a canonical Boolean function, beyond known quantum search and sampling separations.
status_note: Source-open. On 16 September2026 the original full Conjecture3, Definitions1/12, Theorems4/6 and corresponding formal corollaries were checked. importance.reason: A concrete hybrid circuit lower-bound challenge for a canonical function, connecting shallow quantum processing with a major classical circuit barrier while avoiding the ambiguity of unrestricted quantum gate arity.

sentences: Parity is a basic function that small constant-depth classical circuits cannot approximate well on uniformly random inputs.
This project asks whether a shallow quantum preprocessing stage can remove that limitation when its measured output is passed to a classical AC0 circuit.
The conjecture concerns constant-depth quantum circuits with bounded-fan-in gates, followed by the specified classical postprocessing.
Any approximation guarantee must account for both the random input and the randomness of quantum measurement.
Establishing the conjecture would place a concrete limit on hybrid computation and help clarify the power of weak classical procedures that use shallow quantum devices.

definitions:
For \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), parity in the sign convention is \(\operatorname{Par}_n(x)=(-1)^{x_1+\cdots+x_n}\). The quantum circuit \(C_n\) begins in the computational-basis state \(|x\rangle\otimes|0^{m(n)}\rangle\). A qubit is a two-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and the full register has state space \((\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes(n+m(n))}\). A gate is any unitary on one or two qubits, acting as identity on the others. Unitary means \(U^\dagger U=UU^\dagger=I\). Gates are arranged in layers, with disjoint supports in each layer. The number of layers is the quantum depth, at most \(d\); the total number of nonidentity gates is at most \(p(n)\). Any two wires may interact. The ancillary count is separately bounded by \(p(n)\), including ancillary wires that are only measured.

All output wires are measured once in the computational basis. If the product of the layers is \(U_n\), the resulting bit string \(y\) has probability \[\Pr[C_n(x)=y]=|\langle y|U_n|x,0^{m(n)}\rangle|^2.\] There are no intermediate measurements, adaptive gate choices or postselection. No ancillary wire has to return to zero, and garbage is allowed. The initial ancillas are zeros, not arbitrary input-dependent advice states. Gates may depend on \(n\) and may have arbitrary complex entries satisfying unitarity: this is the source's nonuniform circuit lower-bound model, not a uniform algorithm with free real-number input. Consequently no fixed finite gate alphabet or efficient gate-description requirement is imposed.

The classical postprocessor \(f_n:\{0,1\}^{n+m(n)}\to\{-1,1\}\) is a finite Boolean circuit of unbounded-fan-in AND and OR gates and fan-in-one NOT gates, with constants permitted. Its underlying output bit \(b\) is interpreted as \((-1)^b\). Classical depth is the greatest number of gates on an input-to-output path and is at most \(d\). Its number of gates is at most \(p(n)\); repeated identical incoming wires can be omitted. Including wires in the size instead gives an equivalent polynomial-size family, since the vertex count is polynomial. There are no parity gates, arbitrary Boolean lookup-table gates, threshold gates or extra classical advice inputs. The entire classical circuit is allowed to depend nonuniformly on \(n\).

The two stages are composed once: measure the quantum output, then apply the deterministic classical circuit to that outcome. The correlation is the expectation of \(f_n(Y)\operatorname{Par}_n(X)\) when \(X\) is uniform on all \(n\)-bit strings and, conditional on \(X=x\), \(Y\) follows the Born probabilities above. There is no promise on the input Hamming weight. The average success probability at computing sign parity is \((1+\operatorname{Corr}_n)/2\). Correlation is signed; the displayed limit of its absolute value is equivalent to the source's limit \(\operatorname{Corr}_n\to0\). It also rules out a persistent advantage after negating the output.

The polynomial, depth and circuit sequence are fixed before taking the limit, but are otherwise arbitrary. Equivalently, for each such choice and every real \(\varepsilon>0\), there must be an \(N\) such that \(|\operatorname{Corr}_n|<\varepsilon\) for all \(n\ge N\). No particular rate of decay is requested. A refutation can consist of one polynomially bounded sequence and one \(\varepsilon>0\) with \(|\operatorname{Corr}_n|\ge\varepsilon\) at infinitely many input lengths; constant correlation at every length is sufficient but is not necessary for a negative answer.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the quantified zero-correlation limit, or a complete Lean-checked refutation under the same gate, ancilla, depth, size and average-input conventions. A positive result must allow every polynomially bounded number of zero ancillas and every polynomial-size classical postprocessor. Ancilla-free preprocessing, linear-size classical circuits, geometric restrictions, uniform families, a finite restricted gate set or a worst-case statement about one input do not cover the whole conjecture. A negative result must supply a circuit sequence with a proved failure of convergence; search or sampling advantages for another task do not suffice. This is an exact asymptotic proposition, not a request to estimate a correlation at finitely many sizes.

context_blocks.text: A single output qubit of a shallow bounded-fan-in quantum circuit depends on only a bounded number of input wires. The hybrid model instead measures all wires and lets the classical circuit use their joint outcome. The source asks whether this combination can overcome the classical constant-depth limitation on computing parity.

Conjecture3 is a correlation statement over uniformly random classical inputs and quantum measurement outcomes. It is stronger than ruling out exact computation. The source uses arbitrary two-qubit unitaries, polynomially many zero ancillas and no locality or clean-computation restriction; those choices are preserved here.

The source proves a bound of the form \(2^{-n/\operatorname{polylog}n}\) for ancilla-free preprocessing and general polynomial-size classical postprocessing. Its separate linear-classical-size theorem permits general shallow quantum preprocessing, even with quantum advice. Neither theorem covers both polynomially many ancillas and arbitrary polynomial-size classical postprocessing at once.

The ITCS2026 follow-up studies unconditional pseudorandomness against shallow quantum and hybrid circuits. Its introductory comparison repeats the ancilla-free and linear-classical-size parity results. Its broader ancilla allowance for QNC0 alone and its restricted-ancilla hybrid pseudorandomness theorem are different statements from this full parity-correlation conjecture.

This model does not insert unbounded quantum fanout or other large-arity quantum gates. Results about such QAC0 models cannot be substituted solely because both circuit families have constant depth. Likewise, a quantum advantage for a promise search relation does not directly supply a parity decision circuit.
